en: Yes, I would hope so. In a real game situation, you should notice that your foul hitting timing will be longer.
No kidding? Dang, I'll definitely have to try that out.

You've reached a new breakthrough in batting potential!
Your Foul Hitting was enhanced.
Get yourself a dragon from a UFO Catcher. I know that's a crazy sentence to say, but I'm talking about those little action figures over at Club SEGA. Now hop to it!
Back again, Coach.
Hey, Shinada. What shall we have you work on today...
Ah, yes, how about training that will let you hit more fouls?
Fouls? Uh, I'd rather work on home runs, if it's all the same to you...
Now, now. You do understand how important it is to foul off tough pitches, right?
It's an established tactic to wear out pitchers by making them throw extra. You can also foul off pitches until you get the one you want.
Yeah, I get that.
Then quit your bellyaching and work on your timing. You need those fouls to win, too.
Okay, you convinced me. So what do you want me to do?
You've tried those UFO Catcher machines, haven't you? I believe there's a Club SEGA here in town.
I know all about those, but really? A claw machine?
Yes, really. Go play a UFO Catcher and bring me back a dragon figure. I'm sure you'll get it eventually.
Uh... not sure I get the connection. How's that supposed to help my batting?
Ha, your shallow thinking betrays you again. Listen. The keys to winning prizes from a UFO Catcher are sublime control and perception.
One must take aim on a three-dimensional axis, precisely control the arm, and accurately lower it upon its target.
The process, from start to finish, is identical to batting. The batter determines the ball's position along three axes, and strikes.
To get a proper hit, you can make do with sheer power. But deliberately fouling takes more than that.
You need the same precise control and depth perception as you would for getting a prize from a UFO Catcher.
Hmm... I think I'm beginning to see it.
Good, then you have nothing to moan about. Now go on and get me that dragon.
Got it, Coach. I'll be off, then.
You're back, Shinada. It looks like you scored over 800 points at karaoke.
Yeah, somehow. Thought I might lose my voice in the process!
Well? Did you get the sense that your impact timing has improved?
It's hard to say, but my senses do feel sharper. I wouldn't know until I try, though.
Oh, I'm sure you've gained something. Your impact window should feel longer in actual game situations and at batting centers.
That would sure be nice. I'll have to try that out.

You've reached a new breakthrough in batting potential!
Your Impact Timing was enhanced.
Go to Karaokekan in Kineicho and score at least 800 points. Get moving.
Howdy, Coach. Ready to start the day.
Ah, Shinada. Back for more toil and punishment?
Yes, sir. You know I love to train.
Heh, that's a laugh. I don't seem to remember you being very diligent.
Forget it, though. Today, you'll be working on your impact timing.
That's a good idea. I could always use a wider impact window, so to speak.
Indeed. Widening your impact window will help you make solid contact with the ball, even when your swing is a little off.
Then what's the first thing I should do?
Go sing some karaoke. You can do that somewhere in Kineicho, can't you?
You heard me. Karaoke. You know what that is, don't you?
Well yeah, who doesn't? But can this really be considered training?
Absolutely. Singing is an effective form of exercise. Do you know how much energy you spend singing a song?
Couldn't tell you.
It depends on the song, but around 10 kilocalories. For those three minutes, singing uses about as much energy as walking down the block.
And if you give it all you got, your lungs get a solid workout. That's why I recommend singing as part of physical training.
I guess that makes sense.
But that's not all. Karaoke makes you keep time by using your sight, hearing, and sense of rhythm.
These elements are pretty important for batting, don't you think?
Uh... Sure, why not.
Okay. So here's your assignment. Score at least 800 points at karaoke.
That's asking quite a lot.

Indeed. It takes a rigorous mentality to hone impact timing,
especially to the point where you can really see results.
Now get going.
Ah, Shinada. So you've won that game of pool, have you?
Yup. It wasn't easy, but I kept a close eye on the dynamics of the balls in play, like you said.
Well done. This training was designed to help you read the pitcher's motions when you go up to bat.
You should be better at predicting what kind of pitch is coming, as well as the course it takes.
Yeah, I feel like you might be right.
Thanks, Coach. I'll check it out as soon as I get the chance.

You've reached a new breakthrough in batting potential!
Your Batting Eye was enhanced.
Go play pool and beat an intermediate opponent at nine-ball.
It's training time, Coach. Let's do this.
Ah, Shinada. Let's see. How about we hone your ability to read pitches?
Okay, but I should let you know⑬my vision's pretty darn good already.
It's not a matter of having good eyesight. For a batter, there are other visual abilities to take into account.
True...
This time, I want you to play pool. There just so happens to be a table right here.

Will that really help me read pitches? I mean, that's a
completely different game.
Do you know the rules of pool?
Well, sure. You poke a ball with a cue, and try to knock another ball in a pocket.
Essentially, yes. But you also need to instantly calculate the angle for striking the cue ball, as well as its trajectory. Not to mention ricochet and rotation.
And it's pointless to just hit the balls willy-nilly. Each play demands an incredible amount of calculation, taxing your brain and your nerves to the limit.
Huh... Never realized there was that much going on at the pool table.
Well, if you apply all that to baseball, you'll see that it'll help your ability to read pitches.
Based on the pitcher's grip, release, and subtle differences in form, you should be able to have a better grasp on where their pitch will go.
You know... I think you're onto something.
You just now realized that? Anyway, go beat an intermediate opponent at nine-ball.
That should dramatically improve your ability to focus on pitches.
I'm all over it, Coach. Time to crush the competition!
So, you got yourself three home runs on intermediate. Well done.
'Course I did. Simple as a pimple, for me.

From now on, you should have an easier time aiming for
those pitches you know'll make a big impact.
When you go to swing, catching the pitch squarely with your bat's sweet spot will let you hit hard and far.

Mm. Yeah. I'm feeling that. Like, I can already see myself
knocking it into the grandstands... that is, if I were in a
stadium.
Anyway, I'll test it out later, Coach. Thanks.

You've reached a new breakthrough in batting potential!
Your Slugging Range has increased.

Oh, by the way. I was online and came across a website I
thought you might find interesting. Here, you should check
it out sometime.

You learned about Sportsman Web.
...Time to get clicking!
Hit home runs using only one type of swing. I expect you can hit three on the intermediate course. And be consistent.
I'm ready, Coach! Train me up!
Shinada, I like your enthusiasm.
Let's see, how about you try something that will enhance your trademark power-hitting?
That works, but don't you think I'm good as-is?
Perhaps, but strength alone won't bring you better batting.
Even if you have the raw power, if you lack the discipline to control it, then it's virtually a waste.
Well, that is true.
So, your next assignment. Go to Kineicho Batting Center again.
Didn't we do that last time?
It'll be a little different. First, you'll be moving up to the intermediate course.
And second, you're only going to use a specific swing.
You mean, only swing high or low? Something like that?
Exactly. Just be sure to be consistent with the direction you choose. Now let's see... Go hit three home runs.
Isn't that asking a bit much?
For an ordinary person, yes.
Right? So, how about making it a bit more reasonable?
Why would I? You're supposed to be this legendary phenomenon who's overflowing with talent.
Bah.
You'll be fine. Now quit whining and get going!
All right, but I'm still not convinced.
The convincing might just happen when you step up to the plate. You never know until you try.
Ah, you've completed your training. I see confidence in that expression of yours.
Do you? Hmm, I guess I do feel like I have a bigger sweet spot now, no matter what angle I'm going for.
It's not just your imagination. See for yourself at the batting center.
Will do, Coach.

You've reached a new breakthrough in batting potential!
Your Swing Cursor was amplified.
Try hitting three home runs on the Beginner Course, with random pitches selected. That should broaden your range of sweet spots.
Hey, Coach. It's training time.

Ah, Shinada. So it's training you want, huh? You ready to be
pushed to the limit?
Yep, that's why I came to see you.
Very well. You got the right attitude.
Watching you bat, I noticed something. You have a pretty narrow range for hitting pitches.
Maybe you're right. There's usually this little zone where I imagine I can hit the ball. And it's generally quite small.
Thought so. If you don't expand the range of your sweet spots, you'll have a rough time against, say, pitchers who throw breaking balls.
For real... Those guys always throw me for a loop.
If you can't cover more of the strike zone, you'll get gunned down even by beer league amateurs, let alone that rival of yours.
Tell me about it. So, how can I train for that?
Try this. Go to the batting center. The one here in Nagoya, of course.
The batting center? Isn't that a bit... I dunno... obvious?
It better be. Now look, I know what I'm talking about. Try out the Beginner Course.
Really? That only goes like a hundred kilometers an hour.
What, you got a problem with that? How fast do you think beer leaguers pitch?
Around one hundred kilometers an hour...
See? What's the problem then?
...Point taken.
So. Try hitting three homers on the Beginner Course, with random pitches selected. That should broaden your range of sweet spots.
You got it, Coach.
I see you've gone and fished something up.
Well? Does it feel like anything's changed?

I think I can see with a bit more clarity than before.
Is that what you're getting at?
You betcha. Go up to bat right now, and you should notice a curious new ability has awakened within. One like you've never felt before.
Oh wow...
Yeah, let's go see it right now. To the batting center we go.
You haven't completed your assignment. Go fishing in the stream at Mid Square.
Just catch something⑬doesn't matter what. Got it?
All right, Coach. Hit me with the hardest training you got!
I should tell you, Shinada. There's nothing left for me to teach you.

You've grown admirably since you first walked up to me
with those eyes that said, "Teach me how to put my soul
back into batting." At least that's how I interpreted it.
Don't leave those past issues hanging, now.
Well, look who it is. Looking to get trained up?
Nope, I'm good for now.
Mm. Well, all right. Come see me if you do need training, though. I'll be here.
You bet. Train me up, Coach.
While I do appreciate your enthusiasm, there's nothing I can teach you right now. Come see me if you find yourself struggling with something in particular.
Ah, you're back. Well? Kamiyama whip you up some top-tier gear?
Eventually. Sure was a tough slog getting there.
Well, the man makes good stuff. Stuff you can depend on. Make sure you treat it well.
Of course. I remember you were always super strict about how we handled our equipment.

Damn straight. How can you expect good results if you don't
take care of your things? It's like a worker and his tools.
Very true. The pros were pretty fussy about their equipment, too⑬at least the ones who were any good.
Anyone with any kind of sense knows the difference between quality equipment versus weather-beaten crap. I suggest you make an effort to upgrade your arsenal every now and then.
Will do, sir.

Speaking of beefing up your inventory, I found a good shop
online. Here, why don't you take down the address?
